headline: The Planning Board evaluated traffic impacts for a proposed Costco warehouse while DPW presented major FY28 water and capital infrastructure requests.
synopsis: In November 2026, Southborough boards focused on major commercial development review and upcoming municipal capital investments. The Planning Board scrutinized revised traffic modeling and proposed road mitigation for the 167,000-square-foot Costco warehouse and fueling station proposed at 21 Coslin Drive, continuing its public hearing to mid-November. In addition, the Planning Board granted a 90-day temporary occupancy permit for Valvoline on Turnpike Road and approved final as-built and landscape plans for Fay School's building addition. Meanwhile, the Capital Improvement and Planning Committee evaluated DPW's FY28 capital requests, highlighting $1.82 million for smart water meters and $700,000 for water tank rehabilitation. The capital committee also received a timeline update on the Neary Elementary School renovation project ahead of an upcoming mid-November design report.

top_items.title: Costco Warehouse Traffic Impacts and Mitigation Review
top_items.why: The Planning Board reviewed revised traffic modeling and proposed roadway improvements for the planned 167,000-square-foot warehouse and 30-position gas station.
top_items.body: Costco's project team presented an updated traffic impact study incorporating feedback from MassDOT and peer reviewer Nitsch Engineering. Planning Board members and abutters raised concerns over intersection delays, level-of-service failures, and cut-through truck traffic on residential roads. Proposed developer mitigation includes repaving and restriping Crystal Pond Road and Coslin Drive, signal timing adjustments along Route 9, a travel demand management program, and a post-opening traffic evaluation. The board voted 5-0 to continue the public hearing to November 16, 2026.

top_items.title: DPW Presents FY28 Capital Requests and Water Infrastructure Plan
top_items.why: DPW Director Bill Cundiff presented FY28 capital requests and a 10-year outlook, featuring $1.82 million for smart water meters and $700,000 for tank rehabilitation.
top_items.body: The Capital Improvement and Planning Committee evaluated DPW's FY28 priorities, which include two plow trucks at $275,000 each, a $700,000 rehabilitation of the Tara Road water tank, and an estimated $1.82 million smart water meter system aimed at addressing an estimated 20 percent water loss. Discussions also addressed an ongoing evaluation of an $823,000 soil remediation at the former Atwood tank site and the potential creation of a standalone stormwater utility enterprise fund. The committee requested maintenance history records and prioritized lists before finalizing its capital recommendations in December.

top_items.title: Neary Elementary School Renovation Design Timeline Update
top_items.why: The Capital Improvement and Planning Committee received a schedule update on the preferred design report for the Neary Elementary School building project.
top_items.body: The committee received a timeline briefing following the Elementary School Building Committee's October vote to advance a comprehensive renovation with a full-sized gymnasium into schematic design. The project team and architect are scheduled to deliver their report on the preferred renovation design in mid-November ahead of broader joint municipal board reviews. No formal committee action was taken.

top_items.title: Temporary Certificate of Occupancy Approved for 361 Turnpike Road
top_items.why: The Planning Board voted 4-0 to approve a 90-day temporary certificate of occupancy for the new Valvoline facility at 361 Turnpike Road.
top_items.body: The Planning Board reviewed the as-built site plan and minor modifications for the newly constructed Valvoline facility. The applicant planted required donor trees, adjusted entrance curb geometry, resolved a drainage manhole labeling issue, and agreed to Conservation Commission wetland buffer mitigation plantings. The board approved the 90-day temporary certificate of occupancy subject to punch-list conditions, including photometric lighting plans, landscaping details, and an as-built plan showing the relocated fire hydrant easement.

top_items.title: Fay School Middle Road Addition Receives Occupancy Recommendation
top_items.why: The Planning Board approved final as-built drawings and landscape mitigation plans for Fay School's 25 Middle Road building addition.
top_items.body: Peer review engineers confirmed that civil and drainage construction for the building addition complied with town approvals, noting that high flow velocities in an adjusted drainage pipe section will require regular maintenance checks. The Planning Board voted 4-0 to accept the as-built plans, approve Landscape Mitigation Plan Version 3, and recommend that the building commissioner issue a certificate of occupancy ahead of the expiration of the school's temporary permit.
